subject: general
question:
Refer to the following number series and answer the question that follows (all numbers are single-digit numbers only). Counting to be done from left to right only.

(Left) 7 1 8 3 3 1 5 4 8 5 1 4 4 9 5 9 6 8 7 3 5 3 6 6 9 (Right)

How many such numbers are there, each of which is immediately preceded by a perfect square and also immediately followed by a perfect square? (Note: 1 is also a perfect square.)
solution:
**Given: **(Left) 7 1 8 3 3 1 5 4 8 5 1 4 4 9 5 9 6 8 7 3 5 3 6 6 9 (Right)

Now,

Numbers, each of which is immediately preceded by a perfect square and also immediately followed by a perfect square.

So, the needed pattern is: Perfect Square — Number — Perfect Square

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/15f97fd2cc87b2caeb7593c566ce40e40033fe8e019f3088862d4e89628a2cd8.png] 

Thus, there are four numbers, each of which is immediately preceded by a perfect square and also immediately followed by a perfect square.

Hence, the correct answer is "**Option 2**".
